description:
🚀 We are ANVESHANA, a team of passionate student innovators participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are interested in space exploration, AI, programming, web development and data science. Our goal is to turn creative ideas into practical solutions using NASA's open data. We value teamwork, innovation and continuous learning. We welcome collaboration with people skilled in coding, AI/ML, research, data analysis and UI/UX.

ANVESHANA – Different Minds. One Mission!
summary: SpaceLegacy is an interactive web experience that tells the stories of 18 NASA missions whose hardware remains on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Students explore a 3D globe of the Moon and Mars and a deep-space schematic, then open a case file for each artifact: Apollo landing sites, rovers, landers, Ingenuity, Pioneer 10 and 11, Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker and Kepler. Each file has Story, Videos and Discoveries tabs, plus narration with subtitles and transcripts, a mission timeline and a quiz. Every status is a documented mission-end record, not live telemetry, and uncertain facts are labeled. It answers the challenge by turning dense NASA records into an engaging, accurate story for school-age space fans, so they feel connected to the machines that made today’s exploration possible.
details:
What it does: SpaceLegacy is a single-page web app for school students. The Explorer has a draggable 3D Moon and Mars globe, a flat map and a deep-space schematic. Each artifact opens a case file covering its purpose, journey, discoveries, final location and documented status. Narration uses a browser text-to-speech voice with live subtitles and a transcript, or a read-along mode. The Timeline, the 12-question Mission Log quiz with instant feedback and the NASA Sources page complete the experience.

Accuracy approach:

  • Statuses are mission-end records, not live telemetry.
  • Coordinates are rounded and marked approximate, and uncertain items are labeled.
  • Where NASA has no verified video, the app links to NASA pages or images instead of showing a fake video.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with three.js for the 3D globes. Moon and Mars surfaces are procedurally generated illustrations, not NASA imagery. Videos are embedded from NASA channels, with links back to NASA pages if embedding is blocked.

Impact: it gives younger audiences a story-first way into past missions, not a list of facts.
projectRefs: three.js r128 build, served from cdnjs
YouTube embedded player, used to play NASA’s official video
Web Speech API, the browser text-to-speech behind the “AI voice”
Claude by Anthropic, SI assistance for code, text and research
PptxGenJS, library used to build the presentation file
NumPy, used to generate the slide artwork
Pillow, used to generate and watermark the slide artwork
